findings.title: Non-regular FIFO grant input blocks before committed revocation
findings.description: readPrivateFile calls open(file, 'r') before handle.stat(). On Linux a read-only open of a FIFO blocks until a writer connects, so isFile is never evaluated. After valid arguments/auth/readiness, publishing a FIFO grant file hangs indefinitely: invalid raw never reaches publishTransportGrant, the prior active grant remains active, typed failure never emits, and the opened pool never reaches finally cleanup. This regresses baseline stat-before-read rejection and violates the agreed regular-file and invalid-input-revoke contract.

reproduction.result: Timed out with empty stdout/stderr; fake publisher and fake pool cleanup were not reached. Parent killed and joined child; FIFO removed. No DB or provider access.

findings.requested_change: Open using O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK, then reject non-regular files using fstat on the opened descriptor and always close it. Preserve regular-file byte cap and send rejected publish input as invalid raw through existing publisher. Add bounded FIFO regression proving invalid raw reaches publisher, typed failure occurs and pool cleanup runs; no config/publisher changes required.
findings.acceptance: FIFO with no writer promptly fails reader, CLI invokes publisher with invalid raw and cleans up; existing unit/integration/output compatibility checks remain green.
